- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and price is trending down, model frequently under-reacts; add 0.5–1.5 price point lag correction to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 0.5–1% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often over-optimistically assumes continuation of recent trend; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.23 spikes followed by -0.16 corrections, model tends to overshoot; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day after sentiment turns negative.
